newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street shares decline after higher open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street shares decline after higher open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks slipped shortly after opening higher on Monday, as the market remained on edge after Friday's selloff and ahead of economic data due this week which might show signs of inflation.

"There's lots of caution, lots of jitters in the market right now," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co, said. "There is such a high level of nervousness about inflation resurfacing that markets should stay cautious before the PPI and the CPI."
The Dow Jones Industrial average, which sank from recent highs on Friday as a rapid climb in bond yields triggered rate worries, was off 17 points at 8014 in mixed trade.
The long bond was also off opening highs, trading up 2/32 at a 6.63 percent yield.
The Nasdaq composite lost seven points to 1592.
Nervous markets, wary of any bad news after strong gains this year, awaited the release of July retail sales figures and the producer and consumer price indices later this week.
Ackerman also said an ongoing labor strike at U.S. courier company United Parcel Services of America could create some concern in financial markets.
